newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares set for fresh gains after breather.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares set for fresh gains after breather.

text.p: The Brussels bourse will take a breather over the next few days, but dealers said on Tuesday positive fundamentals are still in place and the Bel-20 share index should start probing higher ground soon.
"We will stay around current levels," a trader said. Players were ready to sit back after the recent volatility. Asked if fresh gains lay ahead, she said, "That is more than likely."

The Bel-20 closed 1.20 percent up at 2,398.71 points on Tuesday, drawing support from a higher Wall Street, a strengthening dollar and steady bonds, which in turn were helped by fading German rate rise talk.
"The black clouds from Germany have disappeared," another said. "With a rising dollar we can go back to higher prices."

One trader said that volumes would remain low until early September when most players return from their holidays. "Until then markets will remain tight and moves exaggerated. That is not good for the bourse's image and investor confidence."
"It is best if we go sideways for a few days," he added.
A fourth trader said that investors would remain attracted to shares due to a lack of alternatives. "They are finding low yields on bonds still hard to swallow."
One analyst said that the Bel-20's 10 percent correction since late July had gone far enough. "At current levels the bourse is fairly valued."

"Although further profit-taking cannot be ruled out in the next few days, we would keep portfolios steady," he said. "People who have not got many shares could use the current correction to put some buy limits in the market."
He said he liked quality stocks such as D'Ieteren, UCB, Almanij, Tessenderlo, Arbed and Colruyt.
